register_census_decision: Do NOT widen claim_coverage.py to census the register. The census's own documented predicate scopes it to documents a committed record calls a publication endpoint or a part a submission ships, and deliberately keeps out working notes/receipts/program-memory documents. The register's own frontmatter places it in exactly that excluded class: it corrects no PUBLISHED record, its audience is [maintainers, autonomous research agents], and the manuscript's own §7 table says it is held outside this paper so the paper does not depend on it to be read correctly. It is absent from submission-metrics.json and SUBMISSION-PACKET.md. The actual load-bearing risk (the register's restated NUMBERS drifting from the artifact) is already closed by test_fusion_partner_prose_matches_its_artifact.py, whose BINDINGS concatenate PAPER+REGISTER and are individually mutation-tested (61/61 caught, 0 survivors, at this pin). Additionally checked CYC-0020's specific risk (2): of 116 BINDINGS, 14 match only inside the register; 11 are self-labeled 'Appendix A...' by design, and the remaining 3 were traced individually — one targets text explicitly retired from the manuscript, the other two have independently-bound manuscript-side counterparts covering the same fact. No live manuscript claim is uniquely register-dependent. So: correct to exclude the register, but the exclusion is currently a fact about the code rather than a recorded decision — filed as P1.

p1s.what: The exclusion of the correction register from the claim-coverage census is correct but is not encoded anywhere as a deliberate, defended decision, unlike test_the_census_reads_every_publication_endpoint.py's NOT_ENDPOINTS list, which asserts by name that specific documents must NOT be swept in. Nothing here asserts the register must stay out, or says why. A future session could 'fix' this by reflex (adding the register to PAPERS thinking it's an oversight) without seeing the reasoning that keeps it out today. This is the CYC-0020 open question, genuinely undecided as a matter of committed record even though the right answer (no) is clear on inspection.
